overall_summary: Deduplicated analysis of 47 unique shorts shows a stark performance divide: first-person immersive 'What If You Fell Into...' cosmic survival scenarios and extreme planetary physics consistently outperform traditional trivia by 5x-10x in view volume and engagement (e.g., 800-1,050+ views, 20-38 likes, active comments). Conversely, generic psychology/neuroscience factoids and duplicated re-uploads completely flatline (<100 views). Recent late-September to October uploads confirm that sensory, high-stakes visceral physics paired with 19-21 second runtimes drive the strongest algorithmic momentum.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Planetary Catastrophe ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Titles using visceral descent hooks averaged 800-1,030 views: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes, 2 comments), 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes), and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (823 views, 15 likes).
winning_patterns.action: Adopt the visceral, second-person survival narrative frame ('What happens to your body if you enter...') as the channel's core hook engine.

winning_patterns.pattern: Mind-Bending Astronomical Anomalies with High Contrast Sensory Hooks
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,030 views, 36 likes) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) generated the highest organic reach among non-'What If' formats.
winning_patterns.action: Select cosmic bodies defined by extreme physical contradictions (e.g., impossible pressures, atomic disruption, extreme radiation) that evoke immediate sensory horror.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeated posts about memory and psychology tanked repeatedly: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' achieved only 5, 10, and 53 views across three attempts; 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' scored 38 views.
weak_patterns.action: Halt generic pop-psychology and cognitive fact uploads until the channel builds a broader subscriber base.

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple exact re-uploads ('Why Space Is Completely Silent' posted 3 times: 34, 87, 220 views; 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' posted 3 times: 118, 183, 363 views) yielded declining marginal returns.
weak_patterns.action: Never re-upload identical titles or recycled scripts; iterate only on core hook mechanics with completely fresh subjects.

next_video.hook_style: Visceral sensory stakes with an inescapable countdown
next_video.concept: What If You Drifted Within 1,000 Miles of a Magnetar?
next_video.opening_direction: Open instantly with a POV drifting toward SGR 1806-20: 'If your ship drifted within 1,000 miles of a magnetar, you wouldn't crash—your atoms would literally dissolve first.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the magnetic field is so violent it distorts the electron clouds inside your cells into needles, vaporizing your tissues into a cloud of atomic mist in less than 0.2 seconds before radiation even reaches you.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven 'What If / bodily peril' archetype that drives FACTVERSE's top performers (1,000+ views), introducing a completely untouched, terrifying cosmic phenomenon (magnetars/atomic disruption) rather than repeating exoplanet weather.

Must not reuse diamond rain, molten glass, or liquid iron tropes
Focus strictly on magnetar physics, electron distortion, and biological atomization
